role: Software engineer working on the integration and production reliability of an applied AI document-processing workflow.

sections.title: Project Context
sections.body: The system processes document-derived input and turns probabilistic AI output into data that a production application can consume. This case study intentionally omits employer, client, provider, and document-specific details.

sections.title: Pipeline Design
sections.body: Input passes through OCR and pre-processing before an LLM produces structured JSON. The output then moves through schema checks, application-level validation, and normalization before it can reach downstream application or database workflows.

sections.title: Structured Output
sections.body: The integration treats the model response as untrusted input. Explicit output structure and JSON schema constraints make the response easier to validate, diagnose, and safely map into typed application data.

sections.title: Validation And Normalization
sections.body: Validation checks required fields and expected shapes, while normalization handles formatting differences and converts accepted values into a consistent representation for downstream use.

sections.title: Production Reliability
sections.body: The engineering focus is not merely calling an AI API. It is building predictable boundaries around uncertain output through defensive parsing, validation, error handling, batch-flow awareness, and integration with existing software systems.
